```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.2, out.width = "100%",
  message = FALSE, warning = FALSE
)
library(CAPmethods)

# small plotting helpers used throughout
align <- function(e, t) { e <- as.numeric(e); t <- as.numeric(t); if (sum(e * t) < 0) -e else e }
cosq  <- function(e, t) { e <- align(e, t); t <- as.numeric(t); abs(sum(e * t)) / sqrt(sum(e^2) * sum(t^2)) }
loadbar <- function(est, tru, main, col = "steelblue") {
  est <- align(est, tru); tru <- as.numeric(tru); p <- length(tru)
  barplot(rbind(truth = tru, estimate = est), beside = TRUE, names.arg = paste0("V", seq_len(p)),
          col = c("grey75", col), border = NA, main = main, ylab = "loading",
          legend.text = TRUE, args.legend = list(x = "topright", bty = "n", cex = .85))
  abline(h = 0, col = "grey40")
}
# methods print a small progress line; quiet() just hides it
quiet <- function(x) { f <- tempfile(); sink(f); on.exit({ sink(); unlink(f) }); force(x) }
```

Every method in **CAPmethods** ships a built-in synthetic-data generator
(`<method>_example()`) that returns data in exactly the shape the wrapper expects,
plus a `truth` element so the estimates can be checked. The pattern is always:

```r
d   <- <method>_example()   # data + ground truth in d$truth
fit <- <method>(...)        # run the method
```

Loadings `γ` are sign-invariant, so estimates are sign-aligned to the truth before
plotting; the cosine to the truth is shown in each panel title. The two
high-cost methods (HCAP, CAP-clustering) show their code but are **not run here**;
their figures are pre-computed.

## HDCAP — high-dimensional CAP

`log(γ′ Σᵢ γ) = xᵢ′ β`. With `cov.shrinkage = FALSE` this is classical CAP; set
`TRUE` (auto when `Tᵢ − 5 < p`) for the shrinkage estimator. `X` is `n × q`;
`Y_list` is a list of `Tᵢ × p` matrices. The example has `p = 20`, one binary
covariate, **two** covariate-driven directions (basis cols 2 and 4, with group
effects `−1` and `+1`); with shrinkage on, `nD = 2` recovers both.

```{r hdcap}
d   <- hdcap_example()
fit <- quiet(hdcap(d$Y_list, d$X, stop.crt = "nD", nD = 2, cov.shrinkage = TRUE))

# match each estimated direction to its nearest true direction
Tr <- d$truth$gamma; mp <- apply(abs(t(fit$gamma) %*% Tr), 1, which.max)
round(fit$beta, 2)                    # group effect ~ +1 / -1 on the two directions

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
for (k in 1:2)
  loadbar(fit$gamma[, k], Tr[, mp[k]],
          sprintf("HDCAP γ dir %d  (cos %.3f, β̂grp=%.2f)",
                  k, cosq(fit$gamma[, k], Tr[, mp[k]]), fit$beta[2, k]))
```

## LCAP — longitudinal CAP (time-invariant projection)

A time-invariant loading γ with a mixed model on the log-variance (fixed effects
β, random intercept σ², random slopes Ω). The example has `p = 20`, 100
subjects × ~5 visits, two within-subject
covariates, **two** covariate-driven directions (basis cols 2 and 4); with
shrinkage on, `nD = 2` recovers both. `Y` is nested (subject → visit →
`Tᵢᵥ × p`); `X` is a list of `nVᵢ × q` covariate matrices. Estimation with
shrinkage is slow, so this is **not evaluated here** (~1 minute to run yourself).

```{r lcap, eval = FALSE}
d   <- lcap_example()                                  # 2 covariate-driven directions
fit <- lcap(d$Y, d$X, stop.crt = "nD", nD = 2, cov.shrinkage = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)

# match each estimated direction to its nearest true direction
Tr <- d$truth$gamma; mp <- apply(abs(t(fit$gamma) %*% Tr), 1, which.max)
round(fit$beta, 2)                                     # fixed effects per direction

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
for (k in 1:2)
  loadbar(fit$gamma[, k], Tr[, mp[k]],
          sprintf("LCAP γ dir %d  (cos %.3f)", k, cosq(fit$gamma[, k], Tr[, mp[k]])))
```

The two covariate-driven directions are recovered (γ cosine ≈ 0.98 / 0.94) and
the fixed effects match the truth:

![LCAP loadings, both directions](../man/figures/lcap.png)

## MCAP — multilevel CAP (cluster-varying loadings)

Each cluster `i` has its own loading `γᵢ ~ vMF(γ, κ)` around a population direction.
The example has `p = 5`, **two** covariate-driven directions, `m = 20` clusters,
fixed covariates `X1` and a
random-slope covariate `X2`. `Y` is nested (cluster → unit → `Tᵢⱼ × p`); `X1`/`X2`
are lists of `nᵢ × q` matrices. The number of directions is chosen by a fixed
count (`nD`) or the `DfD` criterion. Estimation is slow (block-coordinate descent
+ vMF + random restarts), so this is **not evaluated here** — run it yourself
(`nD = 2` takes ~2–3 minutes; `nD = 1` recovers the leading direction faster).

```{r mcap, eval = FALSE}
d   <- mcap_example()                                  # 2 directions, X1 + X2
fit <- mcap(d$Y, X1 = d$X1, X2 = d$X2, data.type = "Y",
            stop.crt = "nD", nD = 2, ninitial = 8, method = "CAP",
            H.type = "CAvgCov", Omega.diag = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)

# match each estimated population direction to its nearest true direction
G <- qr.Q(qr(fit$gamma)); Tr <- qr.Q(qr(d$truth$gamma))
svd(t(G) %*% Tr)$d                                     # subspace canonical corr ~ c(0.99, 0.96)
fit$kappa                                              # estimated vMF concentration per direction
```

The recovered population loadings for both directions, and each cluster's loading
cosine to the population direction (their spread reflects κ̂):

![MCAP loadings (both directions) and per-cluster spread](../man/figures/mcap.png)

## CAP-CoC — covariance-on-covariance regression

`log(γ′ Σᵧᵢ γ) = α · log(θ′ Σₓᵢ θ) + β′ Wᵢ`. `X` (predictor) and `Y` (outcome) are
lists of `Tₓ × p` and `Tᵧ × q` matrices; `W` is `n × r`. The example has
`p = 10` predictor, `q = 5` outcome, two CoC pairs (`α = (3, 2)`). The recovering fit uses identity weights
`Hy/Hx` (not the default average-covariance) and `burn.in = 200`; `nD = 1`
recovers the leading pair.

```{r coc}
d <- coc_example()
p <- ncol(d$X[[1]]); q <- ncol(d$Y[[1]])
fit <- quiet(coc(d$Y, d$X, d$W, stop.crt = "nD", nD = 1,
                 Hy = diag(q), Hx = diag(p),
                 cov.shrinkage.y = TRUE, cov.shrinkage.x = TRUE,
                 burn.in = 200, ninitial = 5, seed = 100, verbose = FALSE))

round(as.numeric(fit$alpha), 3)       # ~ 3 (leading pair)
round(as.numeric(fit$beta), 3)        # ~ c(1, -1)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
loadbar(fit$gamma[, 1], d$truth$gamma[, 1], sprintf("outcome γ  (α̂=%.2f, cos %.3f)", fit$alpha, cosq(fit$gamma[, 1], d$truth$gamma[, 1])), "darkcyan")
loadbar(fit$theta[, 1], d$truth$theta[, 1], sprintf("predictor θ  (cos %.3f)", cosq(fit$theta[, 1], d$truth$theta[, 1])), "darkcyan")
```

## CAP-mediation — covariance mediator

Treatment → `log(θ′ Σᵢ θ)` (a-path) → scalar outcome (b-path). `X` is `n × q`
(treatment + optional covariates); `M` is a list of `Tᵢ × p` mediator matrices;
`Y` is a length-`n` outcome vector. In the example a binary treatment shifts the
mediator's variance along one latent direction θ, and the outcome depends on that
log-variance; the true indirect effect is α·β = 0.8 × 0.7 = 0.56. The mediating
direction recovers (θ cosine ≈ 0.99) and the a-path α̂ ≈ 0.8; the right panel
shows the variance score rising under treatment.

```{r mediation}
d   <- capmediation_example()
fit <- quiet(capmediation(d$X, d$M, d$Y, stop.crt = "DfD", DfD.thred = 2,
                          Y.remove = FALSE, verbose = FALSE))

round(fit$coef["alpha", 1], 3)        # a-path (treatment -> variance) ~ 0.8

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
loadbar(fit$theta[, 1], d$truth$theta, sprintf("mediator θ  (cos %.3f)", cosq(fit$theta[, 1], d$truth$theta)), "seagreen")
boxplot(fit$score[, 1] ~ d$X[, "treatment"], col = c("#cbe7d4", "#7fbf9b"), names = c("control", "treated"),
        xlab = "treatment", ylab = "variance score", main = sprintf("a-path  (α̂=%.2f)", fit$coef["alpha", 1]))
```

## HCAP — high-dimensional-covariate CAP

Many subject covariates (`q` large) with sparse, `glmnet`-based selection. This is
the most expensive method (cross-validated lasso per direction-iteration plus
bootstrap inference), so it is **not evaluated in this vignette** — run the code
below yourself (takes ~1 minute at this size).

```{r hcap, eval = FALSE}
d   <- hcap_example()                                  # p = 5, q = 200 covariates
fit <- hcap(d$X, d$Y_list, stop.crt = "nD", nD = 2, B = 5)

# HCAP returns the nD directions as a basis of the signal subspace (any rotation
# within it is equivalent), so compare the SUBSPACE, not individual columns:
G  <- qr.Q(qr(fit$gamma_est)); Tr <- qr.Q(qr(d$truth$gamma))
svd(t(G) %*% Tr)$d                                     # canonical correlations ~ c(1.00, 0.999)
```

The estimated basis, Procrustes-aligned to the truth (each direction matches
almost exactly):

![HCAP loadings, both directions](../man/figures/hcap.png)

## CAP-clustering — clustering covariance patterns

Clusters subjects whose covariance follows different covariate models, sharing a
loading γ, with membership informed by `W` (multinomial via `brglm2`). The
membership fit is slow, so this is **not evaluated here**.

```{r clustering, eval = FALSE}
d   <- cappcl_example()                                # p = 50, two components D2/D4
fit <- cappcl(d$Y, d$X, d$W, ncluster = 2, stop.crt = "nD", nD = 1)

cosq(fit$gamma, d$truth$gamma[, "D2"])  # leading component recovered, ~ 1
fit$class                               # estimated cluster membership
fit$beta                                # per-cluster variance-covariate coefficients
```

The shared loading is recovered; the right panel shows the two covariance regimes
capPCL separates (variance score by estimated cluster):

![CAP-clustering loadings and covariance regimes](../man/figures/clustering.png)

## Notes

- **Bootstrap inference:** `hdcap_boot()`, `lcap_boot()`, `mcap_boot()`,
  `coc_boot()`, `capmediation_boot()`, `cappcl_boot()` add bootstrap SEs / CIs
  (`sims =` sets the number of replicates).
- **Direction selection:** `stop.crt = "nD"` (fix `nD`) or `stop.crt = "DfD"`
  (data-driven via `DfD.thred`).
- **Any internal function** of a method is reachable with
  `cap_internal("<method>", "<fn>")`.
```
